title: next cannot honor its own default limit under the 4 KiB compact ceiling and labels staged changes as byte_budget omissions
outcome: next with the default limit returns the default row count, and an omission says staging when the entries are staged for the next call rather than dropped for budget
acceptance: next --limit 20 on a store with 20 ready items returns 20 compact rows; a changes section staged for the next call is labeled staged, not byte_budget

completion.summary: Made compact next honor its default limit under the shared response ceiling and corrected staged-delivery semantics: the 20-row default survives in bounded JSON/text, future-page entries use the staged reason, current-response byte-budget discards remain distinct, and text never promises discarded entries will be redelivered.
